A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal discovery work, with SITD renamed DR-SIT. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, proofs, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DREAM3 experiments, synthetic causal discovery experiments, sample-size analyses, and runtime measurements in Section 6 and Appendix J.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic and DREAM3 experiments and additionally reports comparative AUROC trajectories over runtime in Appendix J.

M1.justification: The cross-fitted doubly robust moment estimator, nuisance regressions, zero-masking optimization, and paired test are retained. v2's general pseudocode matches the procedure already described in v1 Section 4.3, while masking remains a practical optimization. Renaming and the explanation of regressor reuse do not establish a new underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five DREAM3 networks and the same synthetic data construction across noise levels and numbers of potential causes. The additional runtime curves reuse DREAM3 tasks; moving synthetic experiments into the main text does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figures 2 and 4 add PCMCI to the synthetic AUROC comparison previously containing RHINO and SITD. The DREAM3 Table 1 comparator set, including PCMCI+, is unchanged. PCMCI+ already appearing elsewhere does not negate the added comparator in the synthetic comparison.

E3.justification: v2 Figures 6–10 introduce evaluation of AUROC progression against elapsed training time at multiple trajectory counts, extending the earlier endpoint evaluations. The newly specified cross-fitting count, tuning choices, and lag settings are implementation disclosures rather than evidence that retained experiments changed their settings.

E4.justification: The new runtime trajectories systematically examine accuracy versus computation across all five DREAM3 tasks and multiple training sizes. This substantially extends v1's aggregate runtime measurements and sample-size curves by showing when RHINO approaches or exceeds DR-SIT's accuracy. The synthetic noise-robustness analysis also gains comparison with PCMCI.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports standard deviations for both reproduced RHINO variants and defines reported uncertainty as one standard deviation over five repetitions. v1 supplied only point estimates for these baselines and did not specify DREAM3 repetition counts. This establishes improved reporting, not an increase in runs.

E6.justification: New PCMCI synthetic AUROC curves and task-specific accuracy-versus-runtime trajectories substantially expand the reported results. Table 1 also revises RHINO means: E.Coli 1 changes from 0.686 to 0.671, while RHINO+g on Yeast 2 changes from 0.585 to 0.582, ending its nominal tie with the proposed method. The proposed method's Table 1 scores and all synthetic accuracy, CSI, and F1 table entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 removes stationarity Axiom (D) from the moment-functional theorem, explicitly states the Markov assumption, and replaces v1's scaled-expectation limit with an asymptotic-normality statement and probability bound in Section 5.2. It also analyzes the unmasked procedure's O(dkm) complexity. The principal identifiability proofs, counterexamples, and masking derivation remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the unrestricted claim of needing no faithfulness with a requirement for faithfulness within the target's parental subgraph, materially narrowing the claimed applicability. It also newly claims the first nonparametric Granger test achieving the semiparametric square-root-n rate, distinguishing earlier conditional-local-independence testing. The faithfulness qualification remains inconsistent with Section 4.2's retained statement that faithfulness is unnecessary.

C2.justification: v2 explains that nonstationary applications require checking the Granger condition at all time points and softens the assertion that zero-masking does not hurt estimation to saying it may not hurt. Conversely, v1's Broader Impact and Limitations appendix disappears, including its specific distinction between debiasing the inferred structure and obtaining low-variance estimates.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and a practical implementation subsection specifying five-fold trajectory-level cross-fitting, regressor reuse, validation-based selection, DREAM3 tuning on E.Coli 1, kernel alpha and coef0 values, and lag choices. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's more general implementation descriptions; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked repository's contents.

R1.justification: A new related-work discussion positions the method against conditional local independence, covering Christgau et al., Didelez, and Mogensen and Hansen, and distinguishes their continuous-time targets and convergence guarantees from this paper's Granger test. This materially refines the novelty positioning. The earlier Markov-blanket survey paragraph and several associated references are removed.

P1.justification: Beyond changing the title and method name, v2 reorganizes the framework and algorithm sections, introduces separate consistency, complexity, and implementation subsections, and promotes synthetic, low-sample, and runtime material into the main experiments section. Full causal discovery moves to Appendix H, while the former limitations appendix is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the TMLR layout, redraws the causal graph with additional feedback edges, changes existing plots from shaded uncertainty bands to error bars, and adds compact main-text versions of appendix plots. It relocates the runtime table and adds five full-page grids of AUROC-versus-runtime curves, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The implementation guide, code link, explicit baseline uncertainty, and runtime trajectories improve reproducibility and the evidence supporting computational efficiency. However, the theoretical qualification is incomplete: the introduction requires local faithfulness while Section 4.2 still says faithfulness is unnecessary. Removing the earlier bias-versus-variance limitation also weakens qualification. The net improvement is therefore useful but limited.
